text:
maya: Heads up — saw a perf regression on prefix cache hit-rate after the continuous-batcher changes. Hit-rate for the last 24h dropped from ~70% -> ~41% on text-gen-prod.
liam: ugh, any hypothesis? build+batcher change was the mixing by seq_len bins, right?
maya: yes. We started mixing short prefix requests with long convo requests to improve GPU utilization. But it looks like the cache keying is too sensitive to small prompt metadata.
jonas: can you paste a couple of numbers from profiling?
maya: sure. From perf trace (sampled over 30k requests):
- avg latency (p50 token): 38ms -> 34ms (improved)
- avg token cost: -6%
- prefix-cache hit-rate: 69.8% -> 40.7%
- cache lookup CPU time: 1.8% -> 3.1% (higher due to more cache misses + rehydration)
- KV warmup latency (rehydrate path): median 145ms
- number of unique cache keys churned per minute: 18k -> 42k
sophia: 42k churn sounds like key granularity issue. What are we currently including in the cache key?
maya: current key = sha256(model||prefix_hash||user_id||session_flags||locale) — implemented to prevent cross-tenant leakage. But user_id + session_flags make the key too specific for many customers with per-session tokens that vary even when prefix is identical.
liam: ah. That would fragment hits when the batcher mixes users into the same GPU slots. Any quick win to reduce cardinality without compromising isolation?
jonas: maybe split namespace: tenant-scoped keys for safety but drop session_flags from key for prompt-cached path. Keep a separate ephemeral-cache for session-specific KV (short TTL).
maya: agreed. I ran a small simulation: removing session_flags from the primary prefix key increases simulated hit-rate to ~61% with minimal false-sharing risk when combined with tenant-scoped namespace.
perf-bot: note: change requires KMS/ACL audit to ensure no PII in prefix.
liam: aside from key schema, batch composition still matters. When the batcher groups by seq_len we often coalesce 1-2 tokens active prefixes with fresh long convs which evicts cached KV for the short prefix path. Queueing/affinity might help.
sophia: propose "affinity bins" — when possible, keep >50% of a batch homogeneous on prefix_hash. If not possible, prefer appending small-prefetch windows (e.g., 8ms) to let similar requests accumulate.
maya: did some microbenchmarks on queueing window tradeoffs:
- window=0ms (no wait): throughput up 5% but hit-rate -18%, p50 token +12ms
- window=8ms: throughput neutral, hit-rate -6%, p50 token +4ms
- window=20ms: hit-rate near baseline, p50 token +11ms, but queuing occasionally causes tail latency spikes when traffic bursts
jonas: 8ms seems reasonable as a start. We need also to track end-to-end SLOs — customers care about tail percentiles.
liam: what about prewarming? Could we prefetch top-K prefixes into GPU KV for expected usage windows?
maya: yes — warmup ideas:
1) Top-K daily prefixes per tenant loaded into local warm cache at container start.
2) Short-lived predictive prefetch: when we see pattern A -> B, prefetch B (prefetch probability tuned by PMI).
3) Reactive mini-batches: if a miss triggers rehydrate, spawn a lightweight background prefetch for recent sibling prefixes.

Code sketch for key derivation (proposal):
```
# stable prefix key (tenant-scoped)
key = sha256(f"{tenant_id}:{model}:{prefix_hash}")
# ephemeral key kept separate for session-only state
session_key = sha256(f"{tenant_id}:{model}:session:{session_id}")
```

liam: that should collapse a lot of cardinality. Any numbers on how much memory hits/deltas change?
maya: sim shows active cache set size down ~28% (less churn) and hit-rate up to ~62% with window=8ms + new keying + top-K warmup. End-to-end p99 token latency reduced 9% in sim.
jonas: nice. What about correctness concerns? cross-tenant leaks?
sophia: tenant_id is still in the key. We'll also gate prefetch so that only tenant-owned prefixes are loaded. Prefetch heuristics require audit and a safety toggle.
perf-bot: perf regression ticket created: #INF-7321 (assign to eng-runtime).
maya: next steps I propose:
- short-term: patch keying to remove session_flags for prefix cache (feature-flagged)
- deploy batcher tweak: enable 8ms affinity window behind ff for prod-shadow traffic
- start nightly job to compute top-K prefixes per tenant (K=200) and warm on container startup
- measure: prefix hit-rate, p50/p95/p99 token latency, cache churn, rehydrate count
liam: add a small A/B: 10% of traffic gets new scheme, 10% control, rest baseline. We need to track user-visible regressions.
jonas: also add a metric for "batch homogeneity" (fraction of requests in batch sharing same prefix_hash).
sophia: I'll draft the safety checklist for the warmup + key change (audit owners + data retention).
maya: thanks. I'll open the RFC PR with the config knobs and simulation data. Ping me for SIG review. :thumbsup:
liam: thanks — good plan. If the A/B looks good we can flip the ff quickly.
infra-bot: deploybot: diff for eng-runtime changes posted at https://git.internal/r/eng/runtime/changes/4321 :rocket:
maya: tagging perf folks, cc @perf-bot — let's reconvene after 24h of shadow runs.
jonas: +1
